correctness.rationale: The fixed-force current follows directly from the periodic stationary flux ODE; a sector-centered elliptic Poisson inverse gives a bounded fluctuation corrector and a contrast of sector constants of order inverse flip rate. The exact jump/Brownian bracket yields the coefficient \(\Delta u^2/8\). Jensen establishes the strict ceiling and the high-temperature equality limit. One-sided corner Laplace integrals yield the two signed velocity prefactors and the three locked-sawtooth low-temperature cases. Finite-state and direct quadrature checks in checker.py passed 93 diagnostics. Only the ordered sequential limits are proved. No finite experiment is treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The modern model-defining paper (Roberts–Zhen 2023) explicitly confines its transport calculations to steady currents and finite-interval first passages, and identifies higher observable fluctuations for further study. The most directly corresponding older additive-telegraph ratchet paper (Kłosek–Cox 1999) analyzes mean current, using a depinned driving-amplitude assumption opposite the present locked-sawtooth parameter region. Spagnolo–Dubkov (2005) switches the potential itself instead of adding a constant two-valued force; its rare-flip diffusion limit therefore does not imply the nonzero fixed-tilt current-contrast term here. The pre-existing exact fixed-tilt velocity formula is credited. No searched result with the combined coefficient, strict all-potential ceiling, and asymmetric locked-sawtooth cusp prefactors was identified; broader implicit coverage remains a stated priority risk.
residual_risks: A general two-time-scale Markov-additive homogenization theorem might imply the inverse-rate coefficient as a corollary without using ratchet terminology.
Some older ratchet dispersion literature or unindexed supplementary materials may state an equivalent two-tilt limit.
The full fixed-tilt 2002 article was not examined; only its declared background scope was compared.
No independent mathematical audit or publication-priority certification has been performed.

value.rationale: The observable is the experimentally meaningful long-time spreading of unwrapped trajectories in the same active ratchet whose literature largely characterizes mean transport. A sharp fixed-potential independent dispersion ceiling, a divergent inverse-tumble enhancement, and an explicitly computed geometry-selected weak-noise activation barrier distinguish systems with similar mean current. The asymmetric-versus-symmetric apex prefactors give a precise nontrivial design boundary rather than an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
